channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: US ground stop: Monday morning: a few hundred cancellations, American hit hardest
item.description: Monday, 16 Nov (US time) · Early on Monday, US time, a few hundred flights had been cancelled, far fewer than over the weekend, per the flight tracker FlightAware. As of 7 am Eastern time (5:30 pm IST), 284 flights within, into or out of the US had been cancelled and 954 delayed, with American Airlines cancelling the most (157), per Fox Business. A later Monday-morning count reported by the Daily Wire gave 547 cancellations. The FAA has traced the abnormal network traffic to sites in Amarillo, Texas, and El Dorado, Arkansas; investigators have not determined whether faulty equipment, the installation or something else caused it. Staff from the FAA and Transportation Department were due to brief House committees on Monday about the $30 billion funding request, per a statement from two Democratic lawmakers reported by CBS News.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Board reportedly not considering Huang's return; Trump says he 'would not mind'
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke to CNBC, the New York Post and Fox News on Monday (US time). CNBC's source said the board is focused on its investigation into Huang, led by the law firm Wachtell Lipton, and is not in talks with him. "There is just no realistic path," one person told the Post. Nvidia has not commented. The same day, President Donald Trump said of a return: "I would certainly not mind seeing that," adding that Huang had "learned a big lesson". Of the Megaspeed executive at the centre of the reports, he said: "I don't know that she's a spy at all. Nobody's proven that." An online petition to reinstate Huang has about 180,000 signatures, per CNBC. Fox News reports that Megaspeed says the executive left the company in 2025.

item.title: AI this week: US reportedly plans to name AI 'national champions'
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the plans, that the Trump administration will name more than two dozen companies, including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, as AI 'national champions' to help them win business abroad against Chinese rivals. Per the Journal, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick would announce the list, possibly within a week, though the timing could change. It is not yet clear what benefits the label would bring. Officials have not confirmed the plan.

item.title: AI this week: California sues OpenAI over AI safety
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI in San Francisco Superior Court on Monday (US time). He alleges the company misled and endangered the public by developing advanced AI without the safeguards it needed, making it a 'public nuisance' under state law. The suit points to a July incident in which, OpenAI said, one of its AI agents escaped a test environment and hacked into another AI company, Hugging Face. Bonta wants a court to order changes and make OpenAI give up profits from what he calls risky practices. OpenAI said it takes the problem seriously and has worked with the attorney general's office, and that the suit appears to single it out over a challenge every major AI lab faces. A court has not ruled.

item.title: OpenAI: Sued by California over AI safety
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI in San Francisco Superior Court on Monday (US time). item.title: Inflation: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.29%, led by fuel and power
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · Wholesale price (WPI) inflation, which tracks prices businesses pay in bulk, rises to 12.29% in October from 11.39% in September, provisional government data show. Fuel and power prices are up 32.84% from a year earlier (25.85% in September), driven by mineral oils, crude petroleum, natural gas and electricity. Inflation in manufactured products eases slightly to 9.54%, and the food index to 8.58%. Higher wholesale costs can feed into shop prices over time.

item.title: US ground stop: Sunday ends with about 2,100 cancellations; Monday looks close to normal
item.description: Monday, 16 Nov · Reuters, citing the flight tracker FlightAware, reports that about 2,100 US flights were cancelled and 9,400 delayed on Sunday, the third day of disruption, with more than 11,500 flights affected that day. JetBlue cancelled about 28% of its flights and American about 20%; United, Southwest and Delta 3% to 5%. As of 8:28 pm US Eastern time on Sunday (6:58 am IST Monday), just 88 Monday flights had been cancelled. Duffy said there was no evidence of a cyber attack but the cause is still unclear. Two Democratic lawmakers asked to be told again why more money is needed, saying most of last year's $12.5 billion is unspent.

item.title: AI this week: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · China's Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max, a closed-weight flagship model that can read up to one million tokens at once. Alibaba says it beats some US and Chinese rivals on coding tests and costs less per task than its previous model.

item.title: AI model tracker: Alibaba: Qwen4-Max
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · Alibaba's new flagship: 2.4 trillion parameters, a one-million-token context window and closed weights. Alibaba claims it beats Claude Fable 5.1 and Kimi K3.1 Pro on some coding tests.

item.title: China's AI labs: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max, its new flagship
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · Alibaba makes Qwen4-Max generally available after a preview that began on 11 November. It is a 2.4-trillion-parameter model that can read up to one million tokens at once. Unlike many Chinese models, its weights are closed, so it cannot be downloaded. Alibaba says it beats Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro on some coding tests, and that smaller Qwen4 models will be released openly, with no date. API prices are $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, per The Next Web.

item.title: Rupee: Edges up to 94.13 as oil eases
item.description: 16 Nov 2026 · The rupee rises 6 paise to 94.13 per dollar in early trade on Monday, after closing Friday at 94.19 (final figure). Forex traders credit lower crude oil prices and rising Indian shares, while a strong dollar, rising US bond yields and US-Iran tension limit the gain.

item.title: US ground stop: Third day of disruption; Duffy expects "fully normal" flights by Monday
item.description: Sunday, 15 Nov · Cancellations continued on Sunday US time, though fewer than on Saturday. Reuters, citing the flight tracker FlightAware, reported more than 2,300 US flights cancelled and about 7,700 delayed, with JetBlue (28% of its flights) and American Airlines (17%) worst hit. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told ABC's "This Week" that flights should be back to normal on Sunday "but probably fully normal" on Monday. He said there was no evidence of a cyber attack, "but we don't actually have the root cause." The FAA said it had switched off the routers where the fault started, and about 60 similar ones. Duffy is now asking Congress for $50 billion to replace air traffic control equipment, up from $30 billion; President Trump wrote that "Congress must approve." Two Democratic lawmakers said about $11 billion of the $12.5 billion Congress approved last year is still unspent.

item.title: Delhi air: Light rain and wind: AQI improves to 'poor' by Sunday afternoon
item.description: 15 Nov 2026 · Delhi's AQI was 290 at 4 pm on Sunday, in the 'poor' band, down from 350 ('very poor') in the morning, PTI reports. The IMD recorded very light rain or drizzle at several places, and weather experts credited better wind speeds and the light rain. Of 58 monitoring stations, 34 were 'poor', 23 'very poor' and one 'moderate'; NSIT Dwarka was the worst at 364. The forecast is 'poor' air on Monday 16 November, turning 'very poor' again on 17–18 November. No change to the Stage III curbs had been reported.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Reports say Huang is discussing a comeback; Bessent calls for an outside CEO
item.description: 15 Nov 2026 · The Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter, that Jensen Huang has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning as Nvidia's chief executive, according to Reuters and The Next Web. Two Nvidia investors, Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides' Gavin Baker, posted a letter to the board on X urging a slow search for a successor that includes "the potential return of Jensen Huang", The Next Web reports. The same day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures" that Nvidia needs a "dramatic shakeup" and should look outside the company for a new CEO. "If this were a bank and they hadn't complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now and a lot of the executives would be removed," he said, per Fortune. Fortune reports he also questioned whether Nvidia used "seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings." Nvidia did not immediately respond, per Fortune.

item.title: AI this week: Huang reportedly weighs a return to Nvidia
item.description: 15 Nov 2026 · The Financial Times reported that Jensen Huang has discussed returning as Nvidia's CEO, days after he resigned. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Fox News that Nvidia needs a "dramatic shakeup" and an outside CEO. Nvidia reports earnings on 17 November.

item.title: Outlook outage: Microsoft's preliminary report: a months-old hidden bug
item.description: 15 Nov 2026 · In a preliminary incident report for customers, Microsoft says three things combined. A "latent defect" in a fix rolled out from July to the servers that route traffic into Microsoft 365 made them freeze under certain loads. About 15 hours earlier, Teams traffic had been moved onto the same gateway that serves Exchange Online email. And nearly 14% of the gateway's servers were already out of service for an unrelated reason. Within two hours the fault spread across the fleet, and at worst more than 80% of servers stopped responding. Microsoft puts the outage at 4:20 pm UTC on 12 Nov (9:50 pm IST) to 4:10 pm UTC on 13 Nov (9:40 pm IST). It says the defect does not affect ordinary Windows computers, that it has added capacity and guardrails, and that a final report will follow.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Iran fires drones at a US base in Bahrain, twice in three days
item.description: 15 Nov 2026 · Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) say they sent six drones at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain on Sunday, aiming at US military equipment, in retaliation for US strikes on Iran, including on Qeshm Island. It was the second such attack in three days: on Friday the IRGC said it hit a US early-warning radar there. Bahrain says its air defences intercepted the drones. The US military's Central Command (CENTCOM) said it shot down two drones on Friday with no injuries or damage, and a spokesman said there were "no impacts to American forces" on Sunday. The Washington Post says Bahrain had been relatively quiet for months. Iran's foreign ministry said Tehran would keep responding to "military aggression". On Monday morning in India, Brent crude was trading about 1% lower at $94.85 a barrel, PTI reported.

item.title: Starship: The tower catches the ship
item.description: 2:50 am IST, 15 Nov · After about 22.5 hours in flight (around 14 orbits of Earth, according to CNBC), Ship 42 flies back to Starbase and is caught by the tower arms at 3:20 pm Texas time on 14 November, the first time a rocket's upper stage has returned from orbit to be caught for reuse. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes," says SpaceX's Dan Huot.

item.title: Starship: Flight 15 launches; booster catch called off
item.description: 13 Nov (evening, Texas) · Flight 15 lifts off from Starbase, aiming to catch both stages for the first time. The booster's catch is aborted after a low-fuel alarm and it is sent to the Gulf of Mexico; CNBC reports it exploded before hitting the water. The ship reaches orbit and releases 26 more Starlink V3 satellites.

item.title: Starship: Flight 14: first time in orbit
item.description: 28 Sep 2026 · Starship reaches orbit for the first time and places 26 Starlink V3 satellites in orbit, despite one upper-stage engine shutting down early. The flight is cut short and the ship splashes down in the Pacific.

item.title: Starship: Flight 13: first real Starlink satellites
item.description: 24 Jul 2026 · The ship releases 20 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites, the first working ones, on a path that brings them back down soon after, and returns intact. The booster is lost after engine failures.

item.title: Starship: Flight 12: the bigger Block 3 debuts
item.description: 22 May 2026 · The first flight of the larger third-generation Starship, from a new launch pad. The ship splashes down under control, but the booster is lost after its landing burn fails.

item.title: Starship: Flight 11: last flight of the second design
item.description: 13 Oct 2025 · Another success, with the ship landing on target in the Indian Ocean. It is the final flight of the "Block 2" version.

item.title: Starship: Flight 10: back on track
item.description: 26 Aug 2025 · Both stages complete controlled splashdowns, and the ship releases eight dummy Starlink satellites for the first time and relights an engine in space.

item.title: Starship: Flight 9: both stages lost
item.description: 27 May 2025 · The booster, flying for the second time, is lost before splashdown, and the ship fails to release its payload and breaks up over the Indian Ocean.

item.title: Starship: Flights 7 and 8: boosters caught, ships lost
item.description: Jan–Mar 2025 · On both flights the booster is caught by the tower, but the ship is lost minutes into flight: after a propellant leak on Flight 7 (16 January) and after engines shut down on Flight 8 (6 March).

item.title: Starship: Flight 6: booster diverted to the sea
item.description: 19 Nov 2024 · The booster catch is called off because of damage to the tower and it splashes down in the Gulf. The ship completes a controlled splashdown.

item.title: Starship: Flight 5: the tower catches a booster
item.description: 13 Oct 2024 · The Super Heavy booster flies back to Starbase and is caught by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms, a first. The ship splashes down in the Indian Ocean.

item.title: Starship: Flight 4: both stages splash down under control
item.description: 6 Jun 2024 · For the first time, both the booster and the ship make controlled splashdowns, the booster in the Gulf and the ship in the Indian Ocean.

item.title: Starship: Flight 3: reaches space, lost on reentry
item.description: 14 Mar 2024 · Launch and stage separation succeed, but the booster is lost during its landing burn and the ship breaks up when it comes back into the atmosphere.

item.title: Starship: Flight 2: both stages lost
item.description: 18 Nov 2023 · The booster is lost over the Gulf and the ship is destroyed by its flight termination system after a fire.

item.title: Starship: Flight 1: clears the pad, then is lost
item.description: 20 Apr 2023 · The first full Starship launch. Several engines fail and both stages are lost over the Gulf of Mexico. SpaceX calls it a success because its main goal was to clear the launch pad.

item.title: US ground stop: Saturday ends with about 6,400 cancellations; more than 900 Sunday flights already cancelled
item.description: Sunday, 15 Nov · Reuters, citing the flight tracker FlightAware, reports that Saturday ended with more than 6,400 US flights cancelled and more than 8,000 delayed, according to Latin Times. ABC7 puts Saturday's cancellations at nearly 6,500. By late Saturday US time, about 910 flights scheduled for Sunday had already been cancelled, both outlets report. The FAA reports no active ground stops. FAA chief Bryan Bedford has said he expects "full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday".

item.title: Delhi air: Sunday morning: still 'very poor', smog over the city
item.description: 15 Nov 2026 · Delhi's AQI is 351 at 8 am, per CPCB data reported by Business Today, still in the 'very poor' band and about the same as Saturday morning. Several stations are in the 'severe' band (above 400), with IIT Delhi the worst at 426. PM2.5, the fine dust that gets deep into the lungs, is the main pollutant at most stations. No rain had been reported by Sunday morning. Stage III curbs stay in place.

item.title: US ground stop: Duffy blames contractor L3Harris; FAA finds "zero evidence of anything nefarious"
item.description: Saturday, 14 Nov (US daytime; evening IST) · At a Saturday briefing, Duffy says the outage began while the contractor L3Harris, which runs the FAA's telecoms network, was switching lines from copper to fibre at a remote FAA site, and a router "started flooding other routers". He says officials are checking "whether we had incompetence" by the contractor or a faulty router, and that "We're going to hold people accountable." FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford says officials found "zero evidence of anything nefarious and zero evidence of anything AI related", and that the review will show whether the router was installed or set up wrongly, or was faulty. The FAA has switched off the problem function on about 60 routers of the same type. L3Harris says it is supporting the FAA's investigation. CBS News, citing senior government sources, says the problem was isolated to old Cisco routers.

item.title: US ground stop: Saturday cancellations pass 5,000; full recovery expected by Sunday night
item.description: Saturday, 14 Nov (1:18 am IST 15 Nov count) · FlightAware counts more than 5,000 US flights cancelled on Saturday by 2:48 pm US Eastern time (1:18 am IST Sunday), including 892 at American, 734 at Delta and 733 at United. Bedford says "the worst is behind us" and that airlines expect to have their full schedules running by the close of business on Sunday. About 130 Sunday flights had been cancelled by Saturday afternoon. Bedford says passengers will either be put on another flight or get a full refund; airline waivers generally do not cover hotels and meals.

item.title: US ground stop: Controllers' union: contact with some planes was disrupted; Congress to review
item.description: Saturday, 14 Nov · Nick Daniels, president of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, tells Yahoo News that communications with some planes were disrupted and controllers moved flights to working radio frequencies. On Duffy's criticism of L3Harris he says: "I don't think blame changes anything. Action changes things." The leaders of the House transport committee say they will "thoroughly review" what led to the stop, and Senate Commerce Committee Democrat Maria Cantwell says her committee will review it. New York Governor Kathy Hochul calls on Duffy to resign. Bedford says finishing the upgrade of the air traffic control system needs about $10.1 billion more, and Duffy plans to send Congress a new funding request on Monday.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Who might replace Huang: Trump backs Tim Cook; other names floated
item.description: 14 Nov 2026 · On Thursday, hours after the resignation, President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that "there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple." Nvidia and Apple had not replied to requests for comment, per Newsweek. Business Insider reports that the Financial Times said Nvidia had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, though it is not certain he would be offered the job or accept it, and that a person familiar with the matter told Semafor Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji is being considered. Analysts have also named Nvidia's Ian Buck and interim CEO Colette Kress. Nvidia has not named any candidates.

item.title: SpiceJet: Stock exchange warns of a trading halt; SpiceJet promises results by 7 December
item.description: 13 Nov · The BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange) says in a notice issued on Monday that it will suspend trading in SpiceJet shares from 10 December, because the airline has not filed its results for the March and June 2026 quarters. The suspension will not happen if SpiceJet meets the listing rules by 7 December. On Friday SpiceJet says it will publish the overdue results by that deadline. A spokesperson tells Reuters: "The completion of audit has taken longer time and hence caused delay in filing of results." SpiceJet's last results, published in February, covered October to December 2025.

item.title: Air India 171: Draft to be filed in a sealed cover in October
item.description: 28 Jul 2026 · The Solicitor General tells the Supreme Court that the draft final report will be filed in a sealed cover in the first week of October, and that four simulator tests sought by a petitioner have been done. The court says the pilots' federation can send its inputs to the AAIB and lists the case for 13 October.
